## Lecture 6: Hands-On Workspace Setup {.subtitle}

## Today's Session

**Goal:** Every student leaves with a working rrtools project on GitHub

This is a **follow-along walkthrough**. We will:

1. Install required packages
2. Create a research compendium with rrtools
3. Export Palmer Penguins data to CSV
4. Copy the analysis plan template from Lecture 5
5. Write two unit tests with testthat
6. Initialize Git and push to GitHub

::: {.warning-box}
**Keep up with each step.** Raise your hand if you get stuck.
:::


## RStudio vs Terminal

Each step shows **two options**:

- **RStudio:** Run commands in the R console
- **Terminal:** Run commands in a shell (bash/zsh)

Choose whichever you prefer. Both achieve the same result.

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal commands** appear in blue boxes like this.
:::


# Part I: Software Installation

## Step 1: Check R Version

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Verify your R version
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
R.version.string
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'R.version.string'
```
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** You should see `R version 4.4.0` or higher
:::

## Step 2: Install Required Packages

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Install all required packages
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
install.packages("remotes")
install.packages("devtools")
install.packages("usethis")
install.packages("testthat")
install.packages("palmerpenguins")
install.packages("tidyverse")
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("remotes", "devtools", "usethis",
  "testthat", "palmerpenguins", "tidyverse"),
  repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
```
:::

This may take a few minutes. Wait for all installations to complete.

## Step 3: Install rrtools

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Install rrtools from GitHub
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
remotes::install_github("benmarwick/rrtools")
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'remotes::install_github("benmarwick/rrtools")'
```
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** No errors in the console. You should see
`DONE (rrtools)` at the end.
:::

## Step 4: Verify Installation

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Load all packages to verify they work
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(rrtools)
library(devtools)
library(usethis)
library(testthat)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(tidyverse)
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'library(rrtools); library(devtools); library(usethis);
  library(testthat); library(palmerpenguins); library(tidyverse);
  cat("All packages loaded successfully\n")'
```
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** All packages load without error messages
:::


# Part II: Create Research Compendium

## Step 5: Navigate to Your Projects Folder

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Set your working directory
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
setwd("~/Documents")
```

Or use RStudio: Session > Set Working Directory > Choose Directory

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
cd ~/Documents
```
:::

::: {.warning-box}
Choose a location you can find later. Avoid folders synced to
Dropbox/OneDrive during creation (can cause issues).
:::

## Step 6: Create the Compendium

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Create your project (use YOUR name, no spaces)
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
rrtools::use_compendium("penguins.yourname")
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'rrtools::use_compendium("penguins.yourname")'
```
:::

Replace `yourname` with your actual name (e.g., `penguins.jsmith`).

In RStudio, a new window will open automatically.
From terminal, navigate into the new directory.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** New project directory created with your project name
:::

## Step 7: Add Analysis Structure

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** In the project directory, add the analysis folder structure
:::

**RStudio Console (in the NEW project window):**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
rrtools::use_analysis()
```

When prompted, choose option **1** (analysis/paper/paper.Rmd).

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
cd penguins.yourname
Rscript -e 'rrtools::use_analysis(pkg_path = ".", location = "inst")'
```

Note: From terminal, you may need to specify the default location.
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** You now have an `analysis/` folder with subfolders:
`data/raw_data`, `data/derived_data`, `figures`, `paper`
:::

## Step 8: Verify Folder Structure

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Check your project structure
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
fs::dir_tree()
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
# macOS/Linux
find . -type f -name "*.R" -o -type f -name "*.Rmd" -o -type d | head -20

# Or if you have tree installed:
tree -L 3
```
:::

You should see:

```
penguins.yourname/
├── DESCRIPTION
├── analysis/
│   ├── data/
│   │   ├── raw_data/
│   │   └── derived_data/
│   ├── figures/
│   └── paper/
│       └── paper.Rmd
└── R/
```


# Part III: Add Data

## Step 9: Export Penguins Data to CSV

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Save the penguins dataset as a CSV file
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(palmerpenguins)

write.csv(
  penguins,
  file = "analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e '
library(palmerpenguins)
write.csv(penguins, "analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Data exported successfully\n")
'
```
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** File exists at `analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv`
:::

## Step 10: Verify Data Export

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Read the data back to verify
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
penguins_from_csv <- read.csv("analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv")

dim(penguins_from_csv)
head(penguins_from_csv)
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e '
data <- read.csv("analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv")
cat("Dimensions:", dim(data), "\n")
head(data)
'
```

Or verify with shell commands:

```bash
wc -l analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv    # Should show 345 (344 + header)
head -5 analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv  # Preview first 5 lines
```
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** You should see 344 rows and 8 columns
:::

# Part V: Write Unit Tests

## What Are Unit Tests?

Unit tests verify that your code works correctly.

- **Catch bugs early** before they affect your analysis
- **Document expectations** about how code should behave
- **Enable safe changes** - tests alert you if changes break things

We will write two tests:

1. Test that our data file exists and has correct dimensions
2. Test that a data cleaning function works correctly

## Step 13: Set Up testthat

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Initialize the testing infrastructure
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
usethis::use_testthat()
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'usethis::use_testthat()'
```
:::

This creates:

- `tests/` folder
- `tests/testthat/` for test files
- `tests/testthat.R` runner script

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** `tests/testthat/` folder exists
:::

## Step 14: Create Test File

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Create a test file for data tests
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
usethis::use_test("data-validation")
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'usethis::use_test("data-validation")'

# Or create manually:
mkdir -p tests/testthat
touch tests/testthat/test-data-validation.R
```
:::

This creates `tests/testthat/test-data-validation.R` for editing.

## Step 15: Write Test 1 - Data File Validation

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Edit `test-data-validation.R` with the following content
:::

**RStudio:** Open and edit the file directly.

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
cat > tests/testthat/test-data-validation.R << 'EOF'
test_that("penguins data file exists and has correct dimensions", {
  data_path <- "analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv"

  expect_true(file.exists(data_path))

  penguins_data <- read.csv(data_path)

  expect_equal(nrow(penguins_data), 344)
  expect_equal(ncol(penguins_data), 8)
})
EOF
```
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
test_that("penguins data file exists and has correct dimensions", {
  data_path <- "analysis/data/raw_data/penguins.csv"

  expect_true(file.exists(data_path))

  penguins_data <- read.csv(data_path)

  expect_equal(nrow(penguins_data), 344)
  expect_equal(ncol(penguins_data), 8)
})
```

Save the file.

## Step 16: Create Helper Function

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Create a function to clean the penguins data
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
usethis::use_r("clean-data")
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
mkdir -p R
cat > R/clean-data.R << 'EOF'
#' Remove rows with missing values from penguins data
#'
#' @param data A data frame of penguin measurements
#' @return A data frame with complete cases only
clean_penguins <- function(data) {
  data[complete.cases(data), ]
}
EOF
```
:::

This creates `R/clean-data.R`. Add the function code shown above.

Save the file.

## Step 17: Write Test 2 - Function Validation

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Create another test file
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
usethis::use_test("clean-data")
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
cat > tests/testthat/test-clean-data.R << 'EOF'
test_that("clean_penguins removes rows with missing values", {
  test_data <- data.frame(
    species = c("Adelie", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"),
    bill_length = c(39.1, NA, 46.5),
    body_mass = c(3750, 4500, NA)
  )

  cleaned <- clean_penguins(test_data)

  expect_equal(nrow(cleaned), 1)
  expect_equal(cleaned$species, "Adelie")
  expect_false(any(is.na(cleaned)))
})
EOF
```
:::

Add the test code to `test-clean-data.R` and save.

## Step 18: Run Tests

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Run all tests
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
devtools::load_all()
devtools::test()
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all(); devtools::test()'
```
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** Both tests pass (green checkmarks, no failures)
:::

```
✔ | F W  S  OK | Context
✔ |          1 | clean-data
✔ |          1 | data-validation
```


# Part VI: Version Control and GitHub

## Step 19: Initialize Git

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Initialize Git for version control
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
usethis::use_git()
```

When prompted:

- Say **Yes** to commit
- Say **Yes** to restart RStudio

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit: rrtools compendium with penguins data and tests"
```
:::

## Step 20: Connect to GitHub

::: {.do-this}
**DO THIS:** Create GitHub repository and push
:::

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
usethis::use_github(private = FALSE)
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
# First, create repo on GitHub (via web or gh CLI)
gh repo create penguins.yourname --public --source=. --remote=origin

# Or manually add remote and push:
git remote add origin https://github.com/yourusername/penguins.yourname.git
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
```
:::

::: {.warning-box}
If you get a PAT error, run:
`usethis::create_github_token()` then `gitcreds::gitcreds_set()`
:::

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint:** Your repository is now on GitHub
:::

## Troubleshooting Reference

### "rrtools not found"

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
remotes::install_github("benmarwick/rrtools")
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'remotes::install_github("benmarwick/rrtools")'
```
:::

### "GitHub PAT not found"

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
usethis::create_github_token()
gitcreds::gitcreds_set()
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'usethis::create_github_token()'
# Then follow browser instructions
Rscript -e 'gitcreds::gitcreds_set()'
# Paste your token when prompted
```
:::

### "Test failed"

- Check file paths are correct
- Make sure you saved all files
- Run `devtools::load_all()` before `devtools::test()`

### "could not find function"

**RStudio Console:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
devtools::load_all()
```

::: {.terminal-box}
**Terminal:**

```bash
Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'
```
:::
